title: Baker's Double Crowns TEG 17
title_candidates: The Gap That Would Not Close
Seventh Time's the Charm for Baker
theme: A commanding campaign is sealed with the rarest prize in the game while, further down the card, the final round dissolves into comic carnage.
tone: solemn triumph shot through with farce; exact numbers doing the comic work
opening_hook: Some finals arrive with suspense; this one arrived with a coronation, and a nine at the 10th on the way to it.

round_story.subject: Jon Baker's final round paired two calamitous quadruple bogeys with the best Stableford and gross scores of the day.
round_story.why_it_matters: It is the round that closed out the tournament, and its shape — carnage bookending brilliance — captures how Jon Baker won this TEG: not cleanly, but always well enough.
round_story.shape: A tidy start unravels into quadruple bogeys at the 10th and 17th, either side of a run of good holes; birdies at the 4th and 5th and a strong 14th-to-16th stretch drag the card back to the best Stableford and gross score anyone posted all day.
headline_candidates: Baker Grinds Out the Best Round
Chaos and Class in Equal Measure
round_story.chosen_headline: Baker Grinds Out the Best Round
round_story.standfirst: Two quadruple bogeys couldn't stop Jon Baker posting the best Stableford and gross scores of the final day.

race_story.subject: David Mullin's tidy final round wasn't enough to stop Jon Baker turning healthy leads into a seventh TEG double, while Gregg Williams's closing 29 points confirmed the Wooden Spoon.
race_story.why_it_matters: This is the tournament's resolution: the TEG 17 Trophy and TEG 17 Green Jacket both go to the same man, the rarest outcome in the competition's history, and the Wooden Spoon is settled with a round to spare's worth of certainty.
race_story.shape: David Mullin starts the day only 11 adrift in the Trophy and 8 in the Jacket, still with something to play for; Jon Baker's 40-point round stretches both gaps beyond reach while Mullin's own card cannot keep pace; the double is completed by 18 and 13 respectively, as Gregg Williams's flat finish leaves him 12 points clear of trouble at the bottom.
headline_candidates: The Gap That Would Not Close
race_story.chosen_headline: The Gap That Would Not Close
race_story.standfirst: David Mullin's chase never quite landed a blow as Jon Baker turned healthy leads into a seventh TEG double.

discovered_storylines.subject: Alex Baker and John Patterson both endured chaotic closing rounds thick with blow-up holes, even as the destiny at the top was already settled.
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: It is the final day's blackest comedy: two players litter their cards with sextuple and quadruple bogeys, a reminder that a settled leaderboard doesn't mean a quiet round.
discovered_storylines.shape: John Patterson runs up sextuple bogeys at the 14th and 15th and a quadruple at the 18th; Alex Baker bleeds 25 shots across a nine-hole stretch from the 5th to the 13th, briefly clawing back nine points early only to lose it all again; both finish level on 135 for the Trophy, their rounds a catalogue of collapse.
discovered_storylines.standfirst: While the destiny at the top was long settled, Alex Baker and John Patterson turned in a closing-day catalogue of double-figure holes.

race_state_note: This is the 7th double in TEG history; Jon Baker previously completed it in TEGs 2, 4, 11, 13, 14 and 15.
